findings.title: canManage() grants manage when admin only has VIEW permission on all groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or the MANAGE scope on the "Groups" resource-type resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). VIEW must never imply manage. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() guards with `auth.groups().requireManage()` (the no-arg variant), so an admin who was only granted a view-all-groups permission can create new top-level groups and, by POSTing a representation with an existing group id, move any existing group to the top level (`realm.moveGroup(child, null)`). The interface Javadoc for canManage() in GroupPermissionEvaluator even documents this behaviour ("VIEW or MANAGE"), so the doc is wrong too. The check should only consider AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and cannot find per-group resources
findings.body: Three problems make this method return wrong data: (1) `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only matches the single resource-type resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(); per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource() never get a type set, so they are never iterated. (2) The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz Resource UUID) to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` expecting the group id (the resource name); the lookup always misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. (3) `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authz resource UUID, not a GroupModel id. The result is used by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute and by getUsersCount() as the group filter. Concretely, an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on all groups gets a set containing the UUID of the "Groups" resource, the user search is restricted to members of a non-existent group and returns zero users and a zero count, even though canView(user) would allow them. With only per-group permissions the set is always empty, so the DB pre-filter is silently skipped and results are filtered only after pagination (pages can come back short/empty). The new tests pass only because UserPermissionsV2.canView(user) independently re-evaluates group membership. The method should iterate the actual per-group resources (set a type on them in getOrCreateResource or query differently) and return `resource.getName()` as the group id.

findings.title: getResourceName() has no handling for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users type ("All users" / username) and otherwise returns `resource.getDisplayName()`. Resources created for groups via getOrCreateResource() have name = group id and no display name, so permissions on individual groups (and on the "Groups" type resource) will be presented with a null/empty resource name wherever this method is used (e.g. listing permissions in the admin console). Since this PR adds the Groups type to the schema, it should also resolve the group (e.g. return the group path/name, and "All groups" for the type resource).

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null instead of a meaningful error
findings.body: `switch (resourceType)` on a String throws NullPointerException when resourceType is null. Before this change a null type simply left `name` null and produced the IllegalStateException "Could not map resource object...". getOrCreateResource() is reached from representation-to-model paths where the resource type may be absent for non-ScopePermission representations (throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided only validates ScopePermissionRepresentation), so a client can now trigger a 500 with an NPE rather than a validation error. Add an explicit null check before the switch.

findings.title: Feature check moved to registration time breaks runtime feature toggling
findings.body: The listener used to be registered unconditionally and checked `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` on every event. Now the check happens once at registration, so if the feature is enabled after startup (the testsuite enables/disables features at runtime via Profile.configure and the testing REST endpoint), the cleanup of role/client/group permission resources on removal is never wired and orphan authz resources/policies are left behind. If this change is intentional, the runtime-toggle path must re-register the listener; otherwise keep the per-event check.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. These are distinct permissions (manage-members vs manage-membership), so the doc misleads callers. Also `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a Set.

findings.title: No negative test that view-only group permissions do not grant manage/create
findings.body: testViewGroups grants a VIEW-only all-groups permission and only asserts that groups are listed; it never asserts that the admin is still forbidden from creating a top-level group, moving groups, or updating/deleting a group. Such an assertion would have caught GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returning true for the VIEW scope. Likewise there is no test for an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission making group members visible via users().search()/count(), which would have exposed the broken getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().
